claims.C1: The Transformer architecture comprises stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder.
claims.C2: Each layer of the encoder in the Transformer includes a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a simple position-wise feed-forward network.
claims.C3: The encoder of the Transformer is composed of 6 identical layers.
claims.C4: The attention mechanism in Transformer models is crucial for concentrating on important pieces of information.
claims.C5: The Transformer uses multi-head attention in three different ways, including encoder-decoder attention layers where queries come from the previous decoder layer.
claims.C6: Positional encodings in the Transformer are typically represented using absolute sinusoidal position encodings.
claims.C7: The attention mechanism allows every position in the decoder to attend over all positions in the input sequence.
claims.C8: Additional positional information is required in Transformers since the model does not inherently account for order due to the absence of recurrence or convolution.

claims.C11: The decoder-only model is primarily used for sequence generation tasks like language modeling.
claims.C12: The layer normalization operation is applied in every encoder block in the Transformer architecture.
claims.C13: The Decoder outputs are also caught by Linear and SoftMax layers to compute the final output of the Transformer architecture.
claims.C14: Each encoder layer in the Transformer has a residual connection applied to its outputs to help with gradient computation.

removed_sentences.text: The Transformer architecture comprises stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder (C1).
Each layer of the encoder in the Transformer includes a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a simple position-wise feed-forward network (C2).
The encoder of the Transformer is composed of 6 identical layers (C3).
The attention mechanism in Transformer models is crucial for concentrating on important pieces of information (C4).
The Transformer uses multi-head attention in three different ways, including encoder-decoder attention layers where queries come from the previous decoder layer (C5).
Positional encodings in the Transformer are typically represented using absolute sinusoidal position encodings (C6).
The attention mechanism allows every position in the decoder to attend over all positions in the input sequence (C7).
Additional positional information is required in Transformers since the model does not inherently account for order due to the absence of recurrence or convolution (C8).
The outputs of the encoder are utilized as a representation for input sequences in tasks like classification or sequence labeling (C10).
The decoder outputs are also caught by Linear and SoftMax layers to compute the final output of the Transformer architecture (C13).
Each encoder layer in the Transformer has a residual connection applied to its outputs to help with gradient computation (C14).
